issue.title: sase-spotify: Spotify library reads and gated playlist changes for SASE agents
issue.description: SASE agents of any provider can read Bryan's Spotify library through `sase spotify` and a `/sase_spotify` skill: every playlist, the songs in owned and collaborative playlists and Liked Songs, followed podcasts, and their recent episodes. Library data never reaches a publicly published agent chat, because the CLI enforces that boundary itself. Agents change playlists only by proposing one declarative changeset per task. Bryan reviews it as a PR-style SASE gate in the TUI or on Telegram, and only the option he approves writes to Spotify; that write is re-checked, journaled, reconciled, and verified. The new private sase-org/sase-spotify plugin ships with excellent docs, a strict test suite, and CI. It is installed and accepted end to end on athena.

payload.entry: API contract notes for later phases (sase-spotify, uncommitted until host finalize): (1) Build reads with `library.open_library(config, tokens, refresh=…, use_cache=True, actor=…, guard=…, transport=…, budget=…)` (a context manager). `Library` exposes me(), account_id, inventory(refresh=), liked_probe(), resolve_playlist(ref) (never-guess: ID/URI/URL/`liked`; exact case-insensitive name, then unique prefix; ambiguous_reference or not_found carry details.candidates), fetch_playlist(id) (live and uncached, for apply re-checks), contents(ref|Playlist) (S1, then cache or pages, then S2; 2 retries, then changed_during_read; followed playlists raise playlist_items_forbidden), liked(), library_index() (LibraryIndex.find(title, artist), contains, playlists_with; owned + Liked only), invalidate(playlist_id), shows(), resolve_show(ref), episodes(show, n), search(q, kind, n), annotate_in_library(results). (2) Models carry the JSON contract: to_contract() on Playlist/PlaylistContents(limit=)/Item/Show/Episode/SearchHit, and Freshness.envelope_fields() for output.success. Positions are 0-based. Followed playlists serialize items: null with unreadable_reason and hint. (3) Writes live in api/endpoints.py: create_playlist (always public: false), add_items (1..100 URIs, returns WriteResult with snapshot_id), change_details (name and description only). Scope tuples are READ_SCOPES and WRITE_SCOPES. (4) Apply: catch api.client.AmbiguousWriteError (5xx or a lost response after send) and reconcile; never retry it. Pass budget=RequestBudget(cfg.limits.apply_request_budget, setting="limits.apply_request_budget"). Gate and job actors may wait out Retry-After for up to 5 min. (5) Doctor: PrivacyGuard.evaluate(use_cache=, as_agent=, project_key=).to_dict(); HealthLog().snapshot() gives premium_lapse_suspected(), drift, last 429, and quota; Cache().stats(). Logout: Cache().clear() and PrivacyGuard.forget(). (6) Tests: fakes.spotify.FakeSpotify with fake.client(), fake.library(), fake.config(), and fake.serve() (a loopback server; server.config() and server.environ() give the URLs). It has faults (rate_limit, quota_exceeded, server_error, network_error, timeout_after_write, invalid_grant, expire_access_tokens, login_as), after() hooks for concurrent edits, and the accounts flow: approve(authorize_url) gives a landing URL; /api/token does PKCE S256 with rotating refresh tokens; CLIENT_ID and STATIC_TOKEN are constants. (7) Demo artist renamed "Mara Vell" to "Mara Venn" because codespell flags "Vell". Every scenario is listed in the demo_library docstring. (8) Verified: `sase tool run check` passed (ruff, format, mypy --strict on 55 files, codespell, 533 tests at 97.9% coverage), and tests plus mypy also pass on Python 3.12.

PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: Make the search in_library check cheap on a warm cache — Library.library_index() calls contents() per owned playlist, and contents() always re-fetches GET /playlists/{id} for snapshot S1 even when the contents cache is warm, so every track or episode search costs about one request per owned playlist plus the Liked Songs probe. With many owned playlists, a few agent searches can approach the 200-request budget or Spotify rate limits. Search degrades in_library to null rather than failing. Suggested fix in api-owned library.py: let library_index look up contents by the snapshot_ids of a fresh cached inventory (5 min TTL) before falling back to live S1 fetches.

payload.entry: Phase notes (apply, in sase-org/sase-spotify): implemented changes/journal.py, apply.py, verify.py, outcome.py, drift.py and the hidden gate-only `changes apply`/`changes check` in cli/changes.py (only run_apply/run_check touched). FOR PROPOSE (sase-1rs.9): journal API is Journal.for_change(StoredChange) with record_proposed(frozen_sha256=frozen.sha256), record_gate_created(**descriptor), record_closed(status) (statuses REJECTED/REVISE_REQUESTED/EXPIRED/SUPERSEDED exported); store.journal_status reads the last closed record. Bundle wrappers must exec `python -m sase_spotify changes apply --bundle . --group <id>` and `... changes check --bundle .` WITHOUT -j: they print the bare gate value from the plan table (-j wraps it in apply-result@1/check-result@1). Both refuse unless the change is in the local store with a proposed record whose frozen_sha256 equals sha256 of the bundle changeset.json bytes, so write changeset.json as exactly frozen.data. Apply posts the single superseding outcome row itself (dedup key spotify-apply:<cs-id>:<n>, sender sase-spotify). Test builders for apply live in tests/fakes/applying.py. MINIMAL CROSS-PHASE EDIT: tests/test_cli.py dropped the two apply leaves from the stub list, as earlier phases did.
